doc.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Playing strip shows at McMann's at sixteen and learning to read a show
summary: At sixteen he played strip shows six nights a week, learning from pianist Hill Munter how to read torn, marked-up show books.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You know he can do that really easy. So but that’s when I learned it, I would say that was in high school. I was playing strip shows at that time, I was doing it six nights a week as a sophomore in high school, doing the strip shows at McMann’s, and my teacher, the guy that had a heart attack, that Joey Camara, had a heart attack and they needed somebody right away and my teacher got the call from Hill Munter who was this piano player who I learned a lot from, oh what a great guy he was too. Terrific cat. And he recommended me. He says, “Look he hasn’t got the experience but he’ll cut it right up, I mean he’s a great player.” So they hired me and at that time, at 16, it was legal to do that as long as I was working, I had a work permit and you can work. So I went out and did this thing, six nights a week and besides getting a few bras thrown in my face because the chicks always like to fool with you when you’re young and doing their schtick to you and that whole bit, besides that kind of a thing Hill taught me how to read a show. And I don’t mean a show like when I go out and do Natalie Cole when everything is clear and very succinct, watch the conductor it’s marked right, everything is cool, it’s also copied very well. I mean I played in Bill Holman’s band for five years so I look at his charts, I know what they are. I know how to play a Bill Holman chart just by looking at it. Because Bob Florence, same thing. But I’m looking at those charts, everything is cool. But when you go to read a strip show, where this stripper has been on the road for oh twenty years, or the comedian has been out for thirty years, Johnny Main and all these cats that I backed up. Their books are torn corners, arrows down, scratch this out, put in two extra notes over here, do this, do that. Seg to, and then a name of a tune and what key they want this, and back-up vocalist, don’t back-up vocalist, and so you’re reading words, you’re reading

tunes, you’re knowing tunes that you have to insert on an automatic level, and you’re interpreting this chart that you can barely even see. And Hill just would teach me relax, he says, this is what you do, you go through this number, and I got it down. I mean I was very good at it and I knew all the tunes, you know, playing “Temptation” for a stripper was just remembering what I heard Earl Bostic, how he played it, that’s how I played it. I put the growl in there and just played it like, and people used to flip.
